final_message:
The bug was in `recover` in `billing/dunning.py`. When an invoice was paid and no other invoices were outstanding, the branch that should move the subscription back to `active` was just `pass`. A subscription that went `past_due` after a failed charge therefore stayed `past_due` even after the retry succeeded. I replaced the `pass` with `transition(ctx, subscription, "active")`.

Your reproducing test now passes, and so do the 24 existing tests (25 in total). I saved the test as `tests/test_recovery_repro.py`, so it's a new file you may want to keep, move or delete. I also wrote `answer.json` with `{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "recover"}`.

steps.command: cd billing && ls && wc -l *.py && cat ../tests/conftest.py && grep -n "past_due\|def " *.py | head -150
cd billing && cat dunning.py payments.py; sed -n 85,110p engine.py
cat dunning.py payments.py; grep -n "def transition" -A25 subscriptions.py

cat > /tmp/p.py <<'E'
import re
s=open('dunning.py').read()
s=s.replace("    if not outstanding:\n        pass","    if not outstanding:\n        transition(ctx, subscription, \"active\")")
open('dunning.py','w').write(s)
E
python3 /tmp/p.py; tail -3 dunning.py; grep -n "ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS" -A10 subscriptions.py | head -14; cd ..; echo '{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "recover"}' > answer.json; .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

cat >> tests/test_recovery_repro.py <<'E'


def test_recovery_after_retry_succeeds(world):
    cus = world.customer()
    world.gateway.fail_next.append("card_declined")
    sub = world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 1)])
    assert sub["status"] == "past_due"
    world.advance_days(1)
    assert sub["status"] == "active"
    [inv] = world.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert inv["status"] == "paid"
E
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -3
